headline: Brent ran to $110 while WTI slipped back under $100 — the crude dislocation is re-inflating the tape just as the curve bear-flattens into it.
summary: The new information today is in the barrel, not the bond. WTI fell 2.5% to 99.27 and Brent rose 1.2% to 110.15, pushing the dislocation out to ~$10.9 again — but this time it widened on Brent strength, not WTI panic. Brent is +9.8% on the month, z=0.75, 86th percentile, +81% YTD; oil/gold is +9.6% on the month at the 93rd percentile; DBC sits in the 99th percentile of its year. That flipped the inflation composite the wrong way, to -29 from -26 yesterday, and the 5-year breakeven is +6bp on the week to 2.39%. The offset is real but it is in food and refined product, not crude: RBOB -11.2% on the month (z=-1.13), corn -15.3% with acceleration z=-2.39, wheat -12.2%, soybeans -6.3%, natgas -3.9% today. Cheap bread, expensive seaborne crude. Only one of those sets the marginal CPI print.

The duration relief survived, but its shape deteriorated. The 30-year is 5.42%, -14bp on the week; the 10-year 5.12%, -9bp; the 10-year real yield -11bp to 2.77%; TLT +2.2% on the week. Against that the 2-year rose to 4.79% (92nd percentile, +132bp YTD), the 3-month bill is 4.26% in the 97th percentile, and 2s10s flattened 5bp to 33bp with acceleration z=1.23 — the fastest-moving thing in the curve block and it is flattening, not steepening. The rates composite is unchanged at -58, still the worst score on the board. The clearing price nobody wants to look at: the 30-year mortgage at 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile of its 52-week range, with MOVE at 101.7 and +26.1% on the month. ITB and XHB bounced hard yesterday and are still 8-9% below their 200-days.

What is genuinely better than yesterday sits offshore and in FX. Korea finally snapped back +3.3% after a -18.2% month that still carries the worst z-score on the tape (-2.57, acceleration z=-1.90); Taiwan +1.3%, Nikkei +0.9%, Euro Stoxx +0.8%, DAX +0.6%. The dollar is soft without being disorderly: DXY -0.8% on the week, AUD +0.7%, GBP +0.6%, USDCAD -0.5%, and USDKRW -0.4% to 1325 at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range — this remains a positioning unwind, not a funding squeeze. Crypto has quietly turned up across the board: BTC 83,299 (+2.1% week, +26.0% 3m), ETH +27.2% 3m, SOL +37.0% 3m, MSTR +4.9%. Breadth is still the cleanest domestic signal: RSP/SPY +0.8% with acceleration z=1.70, RUT +1.7%, IWM/SPY +1.3%, DJI +1.0%.

The reasons to stay hedged did not change, which is why the risk regime slipped to -16 from -15. Credit still refuses to sign: HYG/IEF z=-1.21 and -1.5% on the month, HYG at the 29th percentile, BKLN acceleration z=-0.93. The option surface agrees with credit, not with spot: VIX/VIX3M at 0.9115 with z=1.38 and turning up, SKEW 160.4 at the 81st percentile, while VIX is only 17.36 in the 22nd percentile — someone keeps paying for tails into strength. The liquidation in the AI-power derivative complex is untouched: NLR -13.4% on the month at the 0th percentile and 27% below its 200-day, URA -15.5%, REMX -21.7% and 36% below its 200-day, GEV -11.3% and ETN -10.8% on the week. Semis keep leaking (SOXX -8.1% week, SMH/SPY z=-1.11, MU -11.8% month). And leadership is defensive, not cyclical: XLV acceleration z=2.05 at the 100th percentile, XLP acceleration z=2.01, USMV at the 100th percentile, against high-beta/low-vol -8.1% on the week (z=-1.22) and XLY/XLP at the 9.5th percentile. China is the ongoing abstention — Shanghai -0.6% at the 1st percentile of its year, Hang Seng -0.9%.

good.text: Asia's unwind finally found a bid: KOSPI +3.3%, Taiwan +1.3%, Nikkei +0.9%. Korea's 1-month z of -2.57 is still the worst reading anywhere, so this is the first mean-reversion attempt off a genuine washout rather than a continuation.

The dollar is easing without a funding accident. DXY -0.8% on the week, AUD +0.7%, GBP +0.6%, USDCAD -0.5%, USDKRW -0.4% at the 0th percentile of its range, USDCNY at the 0th, CEW firm. EM currencies are not confirming the EM equity drawdown.

Breadth keeps improving with the strongest acceleration in the equity block: RSP/SPY acceleration z=1.70 and +2.4% on the week, RUT +1.7%, IWM/SPY +1.3%, DJI +1.0%, MDY turning up. The index is no longer leaning on seven names.

The long end held its bid: 30y -14bp on the week to 5.42%, 10y -9bp to 5.12%, 10y real yield -11bp to 2.77%, TLT +2.2% on the week. Food and gasoline are doing the disinflation work — corn -15.3% on the month with acceleration z=-2.39, wheat -12.2%, soybeans -6.3%, RBOB -11.2%.

Crypto has turned up as a group — BTC 83,299 (+2.1% week, +26.0% 3m), ETH +27.2% 3m, SOL +37.0% 3m, IBIT +24.0% 3m, MSTR +4.9% on the day. A liquidity-sensitive asset class leading off the lows argues against an imminent dollar squeeze.

Energy equity remains the only cyclical group with intact relative trend: XLE +6.3% on the month with rs +5.3%/+13.4%, XOP at the 99.6th percentile, XOM 98th and CVX at the 100th percentile of their 52-week ranges.

bad.text: Brent +1.2% to 110.15 and +9.8% on the month pushed the inflation composite back to -29 from -26. The 5-year breakeven is +6bp on the week to 2.39% and oil/gold is at the 93rd percentile. The energy re-acceleration is in the globally-priced barrel, which is the one that matters for breakevens.

The curve is bear-flattening and the flattening is accelerating: 2y +2bp to 4.79% (92nd percentile), 2s10s -5bp to 33bp with acceleration z=1.23, 3-month bill 4.26% at the 97th percentile. Rates composite stuck at -58, the worst score on the board. A long-end rally with a pinned front end is not easing.

The housing clearing price is unresolved: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile, with MOVE +26.1% on the month. XHB and ITB bounced 2-3% and are still 8-9% below their 200-days, XHB/SPY at the 8th percentile.

Credit still won't confirm the equity rotation. HYG/IEF z=-1.21 and -1.5% on the month, HYG flat on an up day at the 29th percentile, BKLN acceleration z=-0.93, LQD -2.2% on the quarter. Every breadth signal on the board is being contradicted by the thing that actually funds leverage.

The vol surface is inverting under a quiet spot: VIX/VIX3M 0.9115 with z=1.38 and turning up, SKEW 160.4 (z=1.17, 81st percentile), VIX +2.9% on the week at only the 22nd percentile. Tail demand is rising into strength.

The AI-power and semis liquidation is still running and it is accelerating in the worst names: NLR -13.4% on the month at the 0th percentile and 27% below its 200-day, URA -15.5%, REMX -21.7% and 36% below its 200-day, GEV -11.3% and ETN -10.8% on the week, SOXX -8.1%, MU -11.8% on the month, ORCL -10.8% at the 10th percentile.

trades.name: Long Brent vs short WTI
trades.line: Long Brent vs short WTI: the $10.9 spread is widening again
trades.expr: Long ICE Brent Dec/Jan futures vs short equal-barrel CME WTI, 1:1; retail proxy long BNO / short USO.
trades.thesis: The waterborne barrel is bid and the landlocked one isn't. Brent is +9.8% on the month (z=0.75, 86th percentile) with positive acceleration (+0.25); WTI is +3.6% with acceleration -0.39. A dislocation this wide normally mean-reverts via WTI catching up, but with WTI selling 2.5% on a day Brent rallies, the physical tightness is offshore.
trades.trigger: Today: WTI -2.5% to 99.27 while Brent +1.2% to 110.15, re-widening the spread to ~$10.9 after yesterday's compression attempt. Oil/gold +9.6% on the month, 93rd percentile; DBC at the 99th.
trades.stop: Spread back inside $8.50, or WTI acceleration z turning positive while Brent loses its 1-month uptrend.

trades.name: Health care relative to the index
trades.line: Long XLV vs SPY: acc z=2.05, 100th pctile, rs +6.2% 1m
trades.expr: Long XLV (or 50/50 LLY+UNH) against equal-notional short SPY; add IBB for the biotech kicker.
trades.thesis: This is the only leadership group on the tape with trend, acceleration, and relative strength all pointing the same way. Defensive leadership is a poor signal for the index but an excellent one for a relative-value book, and it is where the money leaving AI is actually landing.
trades.trigger: XLV +7.2% on the month, z=1.65, acceleration z=2.05, sitting at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range with 1-month relative strength +6.2% and turning up. LLY +10.0% on the week at the 100th percentile, UNH +11.0%, IBB +3.2% on the day with acceleration z=1.07.
trades.stop: XLV 1-month relative strength rolls over, or XLV closes below its 200-day (currently 14.8% above).
trades.target: Another 5-6% of relative outperformance versus SPY.

trades.name: Equal-weight over Nasdaq
trades.line: Long RSP vs short QQQ: breadth accelerating, semis still bleeding
trades.expr: Long RSP against short QQQ, dollar-neutral; size 1x. Alternative: long RSP vs short SMH for the sharper version.
trades.thesis: The rotation out of mega-cap tech into everything else is the most consistent flow on the board and it is accelerating, not fading. Equal-weight has trend and the best acceleration print in the equity block; Nasdaq and semis have neither.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY +0.8% on the day and +2.4% on the week with acceleration z=1.70; QQQ/SPY -1.4% on the month; SMH/SPY z=-1.11 with acceleration -0.92; SOXX -8.1% on the week, AVGO -6.4%, MU -6.0%.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY 1-month turns positive, or RSP/SPY acceleration falls back below zero on a week of QQQ outperformance.

trades.name: AI-power derivative complex
trades.line: Short GEV and the nuclear/grid complex: no bid, 0th percentile
trades.expr: Short GEV outright (or Jan puts ~10% OTM), paired with a short in NLR; keep ETN and CEG on the same leash.
trades.thesis: The power-for-AI trade is being unwound by the same money that is selling semis, and it has no valuation floor and no natural buyer. Every leg of the complex is in a down or rolling-over trend with 52-week percentiles at or near zero.
trades.trigger: GEV -11.3% on the week, -17.5% on the quarter, 3-month relative strength -19.9%. NLR -13.4% on the month at the 0th percentile, 27% below its 200-day; URA -15.5%; REMX -21.7%; GRID -5.6% with z=-1.19; ETN -10.8% on the week with z=-1.61; CEG -12.5%.
trades.stop: GEV reclaims its 200-day (4.8% above spot) or NLR turns its 1-month trend up — that would mark the unwind as complete.

trades.name: Brazil equities
trades.line: Long EWZ: +14.4% 1m, z=1.65, BRL firming into it
trades.expr: Long EWZ outright, unhedged (the currency is working for you); add BVSP futures for size.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the one EM where equity strength and currency strength are moving together, which is what separates a real re-rating from a dollar-funded bounce. It is also a direct beneficiary of a $110 Brent print.
trades.trigger: EWZ +2.4% on the day, +14.4% on the month (z=1.65), +20.6% on the quarter, 1-month relative strength +13.3% and turning up; BVSP z=2.12 at the 99th percentile; USDBRL -2.5% on the month at the 16th percentile and rolling over.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.25, or EWZ losing its 200-day (16.5% below spot).

trades.name: Index tail hedge
trades.line: Buy Dec SPX put spread: SKEW 160, VIX curve inverting
trades.expr: Buy SPX Dec 7400/6900 put spread financed partly by selling a 1-month 8100 call; or VIX Dec 20/30 call spread. Size to 60-80bp of book.
trades.thesis: Spot vol is cheap and the surface is not. Credit, the VIX term structure and SKEW are all signalling the same thing the index refuses to price, with SPX at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.trigger: VIX/VIX3M at 0.9115, z=1.38 and turning up with acceleration 0.76, while VIX sits at 17.36 in the 22nd percentile; SKEW 160.4 (z=1.17, 81st percentile); HYG/IEF z=-1.21 falling on up days; rates composite -58 and mortgage rates at a 100th-percentile 7.40%.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.85 with HYG/IEF z above zero — that combination means credit has finally confirmed and the hedge is dead weight.
trades.target: VIX 24 / a 5% SPX drawdown pays the structure 3-4x.

trades.name: Short USD/MXN
trades.line: Short USDMXN: z=2.67, the most stretched move on the board
trades.expr: Short USDMXN spot/forward, 1-3 month, or buy 3-month MXN calls; size small given carry-adjusted gap risk.
trades.thesis: The peso sell-off is not being confirmed by anything else in Mexico or in EM FX generally. Local equity is making highs while the currency makes lows — one of them is wrong, and the carry is on the fade.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +7.3% on the month with z=2.67 and acceleration z=1.34, 5.85% above its 200-day — the largest z-score anywhere in the digest — while MXX is +9.3% on the month (z=2.00) and EWW +3.1% on the week, with CEW firm and USDBRL/USDKRW both falling.
trades.stop: 19.00 spot: above that this is a genuine local-risk event, not positioning, and the trade is wrong.
